question: A tennis server wins 55% of points, each independently. About what share of service games does he win?
answer: About 62%. A game needs four points and a two-point margin, so a small edge on each point compounds: all the paths through 40-15 and deuce are tilted the same way. At 60% of points the figure is about 74%. Sets and matches magnify it again, which is how small edges become lopsided scorelines.
move: A small edge repeated through a winner-takes-all format becomes a large one.
trap: Expecting the share of games to mirror the share of points.
source: Newton & Keller, Studies in Applied Mathematics, 2005
reference: Newton & Keller, Probability of winning at tennis I. Theory and data, Studies in Applied Mathematics, 2005
